import markdown
import os

def test_subdirectory_imports():
    """Test that subdirectory imports work with restrict_base_path=True"""
    
    # Change to the test directory
    test_dir = '/tmp/test_docs'

    print(f"Contents of includes directory: {os.listdir('includes')}")
    
    # Read the parent file
    with open('parent-file.md', 'r') as f:
        md_content = f.read()
    
    print("\nOriginal markdown content:")
    print(md_content)
    
    # Configure markdown with snippets extension
    md = markdown.Markdown(extensions=['pymdownx.snippets'])
    md.set_output_format('html')
    
    # Configure snippets with base_path and restrict_base_path
    md.parser.extensions['pymdownx.snippets'].config = {
        'base_path': [['.'], 'Base path for snippet paths'],
        'restrict_base_path': [True, 'Restrict snippet paths to base path'],
        'check_paths': [True, 'Make the build fail if a snippet can\'t be found']
    }
    
    # Reset the preprocessor to pick up new config
    md.preprocessors.deregister('snippet')
    from pymdownx.snippets import SnippetPreprocessor
    snippet_preprocessor = SnippetPreprocessor(md)
    snippet_preprocessor.config = md.parser.extensions['pymdownx.snippets'].config
    md.preprocessors.register(snippet_preprocessor, 'snippet', 32)
    
    try:
        # Process the markdown
        html_output = md.convert(md_content)
        print("\nGenerated HTML:")
        print(html_output)
        print("\nSUCCESS: Subdirectory imports worked!")

#!/usr/bin/env python3

"""
Unit test for the audience null fix that could be integrated into the test suite.
"""

import jwt
import pytest


def test_decode_with_aud_null_and_no_audience():
    """Test that JWT with {"aud": null} is treated same as no aud claim when no audience is specified."""
    payload = {"some": "payload", "aud": None}
    secret = "secret"
    token = jwt.encode(payload, secret, algorithm="HS256")
    
    # Should decode successfully without audience parameter
    decoded = jwt.decode(token, secret, algorithms=["HS256"])
    assert decoded["some"] == "payload"
    assert decoded["aud"] is None


def test_decode_with_aud_null_and_audience_specified():
    """Test that JWT with {"aud": null} fails appropriately when audience is specified."""
    payload = {"some": "payload", "aud": None}
    secret = "secret"
    token = jwt.encode(payload, secret, algorithm="HS256")
    
    # Should raise MissingRequiredClaimError when audience is expected but aud is null
    with pytest.raises(jwt.MissingRequiredClaimError) as exc_info:
        jwt.decode(token, secret, audience="urn:test", algorithms=["HS256"])
    
    assert exc_info.value.claim == "aud"


def test_decode_with_aud_null_and_verify_aud_false():
    """Test that JWT with {"aud": null} works when aud verification is disabled."""
    payload = {"some": "payload", "aud": None}
    secret = "secret"
    token = jwt.encode(payload, secret, algorithm="HS256")
    
    # Should decode successfully when aud verification is disabled
    decoded = jwt.decode(
        token, 
        secret, 
        options={"verify_aud": False}, 
        algorithms=["HS256"]
    )
    assert decoded["some"] == "payload"
    assert decoded["aud"] is None


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Run the tests
    test_decode_with_aud_null_and_no_audience()
    print("✅ test_decode_with_aud_null_and_no_audience passed")
    
    test_decode_with_aud_null_and_audience_specified()
    print("✅ test_decode_with_aud_null_and_audience_specified passed")
    
    test_decode_with_aud_null_and_verify_aud_false()
    print("✅ test_decode_with_aud_null_and_verify_aud_false passed")
    
    print("🎉 All tests passed!")

     1	# Shrink Ray
     2	
     3	Shrink Ray is a modern multiformat test-case reducer.
     4	
     5	It's designed to be highly parallel, and work with a very wide variety of formats, through a mix of good generic algorithms and format-specific reduction passes.
     6	
     7	## Disclaimers about quality
     8	
     9	Currently shrink ray is in a very alpha quality state. I expect it to mostly work for most use cases, but also is probably super buggy in ways I've not discovered yet. I encourage people to try it out, but also please let me know when it inevitably breaks, or if it doesn't produce very good results for your use cases.
    10	
    11	Additionally, this is a "prerelease" version in the sense that there is no official release yet and you're expected to just run off main (don't worry this is easy to do). Unfortunately that means I'll occasionally break things I didn't mean to. The goal is to have Shrink Ray on a more sensible release and development schedule by mid 2024 at the latest, but it's very much not there yet.
    12	
    13	All this being said this probably doesn't matter that much for the question of whether to give it a go. It's in the nature of test-case reduction that it doesn't matter all that much if it's bad, because it's still going to do a bunch of work that you didn't have to do by hand. Try it out, see if it works. If it doesn't, please tell me and I'll make it work better.
    14	
    15	## Installation
    16	
    17	Shrink Ray requires Python 3.12 or later, and can be installed using pip.
    18	
    19	There is currently no official release for shrink ray, and I recommend running off main. You can install it as follows:
    20	
    21	```
    22	pipx install git+https://github.com/DRMacIver/shrinkray.git
    23	```
    24	
    25	(if you don't have or want [pipx](https://pypa.github.io/pipx/) you could also do this with pip and it would work fine)
    26	
    27	Shrink Ray requires Python 3.12 or later and won't work on earlier versions. If everything is working correctly, it should refuse to install
    28	on versions it's incompatible with. If you do not have Python 3.12 installed, I recommend [pyenv](https://github.com/pyenv/pyenv) for managing
    29	Python installs.
    30	
    31	If you want to use it from the git repo directly, you can do the following:
    32	
    33	```
    34	git checkout https://github.com/DRMacIver/shrinkray.git
    35	cd shrinkray
    36	virtualenv .venv
    37	.venv/bin/pip install -e .
    38	```
    39	
    40	You will now have a shrinkray executable in .venv/bin, which you can also put on your path by running `source .venv/bin/activate`.
    41	
    42	## Usage
    43	
    44	Shrink Ray is run as follows:
    45	
    46	```
    47	shrinkray is_interesting.sh my-test-case
    48	```
    49	
    50	Where `my-test-case` is some file you want to reduce and `is_interesting.sh` can be any executable that exits with `0` when a test case passed to it is interesting and non-zero otherwise.
    51	
    52	Variant test cases are passed to the interestingness test both on STDIN and as a file name passed as an argument. Additionally for creduce compatibility, the file has the same base name as the original test case and is in the current working directory the script is run with. This behaviour can be customised with the `--input-type` argument.
    53	
    54	`shrinkray --help` will give more usage instructions.
    55	
    56	## Supported formats
    57	
    58	Shrink Ray is fully generic in the sense that it will work with literally any file you give it in any format. However, some formats will work a lot better than others.
    59	
    60	It has a generic reduction algorithm that should work pretty well with any textual format, and an architecture that is designed to make it easy to add specialised support for specific formats as needed.
    61	
    62	Additionally, Shrink Ray has special support for the following formats:
    63	
    64	* C and C++ (via `clang_delta`, which you will have if creduce is installed)
    65	* Python (Quite basic support, but easy to improve)
    66	
    67	It is fairly easy to add support for new formats as needed.
    68	If you run into a test case and interestingness test that you care about that shrink ray handles badly please let me know and I'll likely see about improving its handling of that format.
    69	
    70	## Parallelism
    71	
    72	You can control the number of parallel tasks shrinkray will run with the `--parallelism` flag. By default this will be the number of CPU cores you have available
    73	
    74	Shrink Ray is designed to be able to run heavily in parallel, with a basic heuristic of aiming to be embarrassingly parallel when making no progress, mostly sequential when making progress, and smoothly scaling in between the two. It mostly succeeds at this.
    75	
    76	Currently the bottleneck on scaling to a very large number of cores is how fast the controlling Python program can generate variant test cases to try and pass them to the interestingness test. This isn't well optimised at present and I don't currently have good benchmarks for it, but I'd expect you to be able to get linear speedups on most workflows while running 10-20 test cases in parallel, and to start to struggle past that.
    77	
    78	This also depends on the performance of the interestingness test - the slower your test is to run, the more you'll be able to scale linearly with the number of cores available.
    79	
    80	I'm quite interested in getting this part to scale well, so please let me know if you find examples where it doesn't seem to work.
    81	
    82	## Bug Reports
    83	
    84	Shrink Ray is still pretty new and under-tested software, so it definitely has bugs. If you run into any, [please file an issue](https://github.com/DRMacIver/shrinkray/issues).
    85	
    86	As well as obvious bugs (crashes, etc) I'm also very interested in hearing about usability issues and cases where the reduced test case isn't very good.
    87	
    88	Requests for new features, new supported formats, etc. also welcome although I'm less likely to jump right on them.
